blocks.html: Enterprise Value (EV) is a comprehensive measure of a company’s total value, calculated by combining market capitalization with debt and subtracting cash and cash equivalents.

EV provides a more accurate representation of a company’s overall valuation than market capitalization alone. It reflects the total cost to acquire a business, as it accounts for both its equity value and outstanding obligations while considering available cash.
Enterprise Value is calculated using the following formula:

items.html: (Market Capitalization + Total Debt − Cash and Cash Equivalents)

items.title: Market Capitalization
items.html: represents the total value of a company’s outstanding shares

items.title: Total Debt
items.html: includes both short-term and long-term liabilities

items.title: Cash and Cash Equivalents
items.html: are subtracted as they reduce the net acquisition cost

blocks.html: Provides a holistic view of a company’s valuation
Enables better comparison across companies with different capital structures
Helps investors assess acquisition costs more accurately
Supports financial modeling and investment decisions
Offers deeper insights than market cap alone
EV is commonly used in financial analysis, especially in valuation multiples like EV/EBITDA.
If a company has a market capitalization of ₹500 crore, total debt of ₹200 crore, and cash reserves of ₹100 crore, its Enterprise Value would be ₹600 crore.

Enterprise Value is a key financial metric for understanding the true worth of a business. By factoring in debt and cash, it offers a more complete picture of a company’s value and investment potential.
